new_scholarship.name: Overseas Scholarship for MS/M.Phil and Ph.D Studies (Phase-III), Higher Education Commission Pakistan
new_scholarship.description: The Higher Education Commission of Pakistan awards MS/M.Phil and PhD scholarships to Pakistani and Azad Jammu and Kashmir nationals to study at universities ranked in the top 200 of the QS or THE world rankings, in eight named thematic areas. Payments cover a maintenance allowance, a capped contribution to tuition fees, health insurance and one economy-class round-trip air ticket. Admission to the foreign university is separate from the award and must be secured by the scholar. The Batch-IV application window ran from 9 August 2026 to 28 August 2026 and has closed; HEC runs the scheme in successive batches.
new_scholarship.duration: Maintenance allowance payable for up to 24 months for the MS program and up to 48 months for the PhD program; tuition contribution capped at two years for MS and four years for PhD.
new_scholarship.application_period: Batch-IV online registration 9 August 2026 to 28 August 2026 16:00, with the HEC Aptitude Test held 27 September 2026; further batches announced by HEC
funding_coverage: Maintenance allowance up to USD 1,600 per month, or the approved country stipend rate, covering accommodation, course literature, visa expenses and other approved living expenses
Up to USD 4,000 per annum towards tuition fees for a maximum of two years (MS) or four years (PhD)
Health insurance reimbursed on an actual-cost basis up to USD 600 per annum
One economy-class round-trip air ticket reimbursed on an actual-cost basis, subject to a maximum of PKR 250,000 one-way
eligibility: Pakistani or Azad Jammu and Kashmir national
Minimum CGPA 3.0 out of 4.0 for MS applicants and for PhD applicants in their MS/MPhil
At most one second division (or equivalent) in the academic career before the terminal degree
For PhD: minimum 18 years of education, or 17 years with equivalence from the HEC Assessment and Accreditation division
Age limit 30 for MS and 35 for PhD for non-government employees; 35 for MS and 40 for PhD for public-sector, government or semi-government employees
Employees of public-sector universities, colleges, R&D bodies or government organisations must submit a No Objection Certificate
A valid HEC Aptitude Test score is required unless exempt
requirements: Online registration through the HEC e-Services Scholarship Portal
Application processing fee of Rs. 3,000 paid through 1LINK payment services
A valid HEC Aptitude Test score valid for two years
Confirmed admission offer from a top-200 QS/THE ranked university in a thematic area
application_method: Register online through the HEC e-Services Scholarship Portal
Pay the Rs. 3,000 processing fee through 1LINK payment services
Sit the HEC Aptitude Test (HAT) conducted by the Education Testing Council
Attend the interview if shortlisted
new_scholarship.selection_notes: Selection is on merit based on HEC Aptitude Test scores and interview results, subject to approved provincial quotas and thematic-area slot availability. Candidates holding confirmed unconditional admission in a thematic area for Fall 2026 at a top-200 QS/THE ranked university are exempted from the scholarship test and interview. HEC may re-allocate the chosen university or country.
new_scholarship.english_requirement_note: HEC does not state an English test requirement for the scholarship itself, but requires candidates to meet the host university's admission requirements, which may include GRE, TOEFL or IELTS.
award_holder_conditions: Applicants sign a Deed of Agreement and Surety Bond and an Undertaking covering service and assets
Previous HEC-funded MS/MPhil recipients must complete a two-year residency period in Pakistan before re-applying for a PhD award
new_scholarship.notes: Tuition support is capped rather than full: HEC states that any tuition fee exceeding the allocated amount must be covered by a fee waiver or by the scholar.

new_scholarship.name: Scholarships for Staff and Instructors' Knowledge Advancement Program (SIKAP), Commission on Higher Education Philippines
new_scholarship.description: SIKAP is the Commission on Higher Education's principal graduate scholarship programme, funding teaching and non-teaching staff of Philippine higher education institutions to study for a Master's or Doctorate in one of ten priority disciplines within the Philippines. CHED pays tuition and other fees at actual cost and adds a monthly stipend plus a research allowance. Applicants are nominated through their employing institution, and awards are made in numbered batches against the CHED Regional Offices. The 2026 Call Cycle is open and Batch 5 closes on 5 October 2026.
new_scholarship.duration: Full-time or part-time study; CHED does not publish a fixed maximum duration on the programme pages read.

Research allowance of PHP 150,000 for Master's and PHP 250,000 for Doctorate study

new_scholarship.name: TaiwanICDF Scholarship Program (International Higher Education Scholarship Program), TaiwanICDF
new_scholarship.official_source: International Cooperation and Development Fund (TaiwanICDF), Taiwan
new_scholarship.description: The TaiwanICDF Scholarship is the International Cooperation and Development Fund's International Higher Education Scholarship Program, which the Fund describes as offering full scholarships to outstanding students from partner countries to study in Taiwan through its TICA network of partner universities. Applicants apply to one programme at one TICA university per year through the Fund's online application system. programme_detail_official.description: The Allama Muhammad Iqbal Scholarship for Central Asia and Friendly Countries is a Government of Pakistan scholarship administered by the Higher Education Commission. HEC states that over five years the programme will offer 350 scholarships to international students from Central Asian and friendly countries to pursue undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral degrees at top-ranked Pakistani universities. programme_detail_official.description: The Allama Muhammad Iqbal Scholarships for Students from Bangladesh are the fully funded student awards of the Government of Pakistan's Pak-Bangladesh Knowledge Corridor, administered by the Higher Education Commission. HEC offers 500 scholar places to Bangladeshi citizens at Bachelor's, Master's and PhD level across medicine, engineering, computer science, business administration, mass communication, media studies and the basic and social sciences, at Pakistani public and private universities. Benefits cover full tuition, a stipend, hostel and mess charges, a settlement allowance, an air ticket, and books and stationery. Entry thresholds are 60% for the general Bachelor's programme, 65% Pre-Medical for medicine, dentistry and pharmacy, 65% Pre-Engineering for engineering, and 3.00 CGP or 65% for postgraduate and doctoral study, with ages 17 to 23 for BS and a maximum of 35 for doctoral awards. Recipients are required to serve Bangladesh after completing their education in Pakistan.
